answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card, adding one per fatigue and another for Chairman. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire the officeholder to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner may select or discard a display card. They act in descending actual retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards during selection; if empty, skip remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown). Return all unused Pensioners to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season, Retirements; Prestige.

answers.answer: At phase start check whether the opportunity marker already matches the chosen main action. If so, that action may be taken twice; otherwise once. Move the marker onto the chosen action. Only the latest passed extra-action law can grant an extra action; it is not doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices, a doubled Enlist Writer can place three writers total: the vacancy bonus is one additional writer once this turn, not once per action.

After family actions, while Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Initial application payments go to the bank, never Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family, New Company shares.

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending number on card backs. Own-family ordinary hiring requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. When promoting an officeholder, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card into ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip it; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

Former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody gets that support, former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including self. The winner’s share moves to the Chairman slot and still counts for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.

Pay all Company-check cash from the acting office’s treasury to the bank before rolling. Gather dice and subtract penalties; the lowest die governs: 1–2 success, 3–4 failure (retry if resources and office limits permit), 5–6 catastrophe (no more office actions; return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue, flip card into Vacant Offices). Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying with no dice to trigger officer losses.

Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each further advance needs consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting Chairman; never advance past the Debt track end. Allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved within these limits; money already in offices remains there.

Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It can lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put acquired ships in any sea zone, including China once it exists. Leased extra ships return at Refresh.

Declare home region plus only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Pay £1 from President’s treasury per die, subtract one die per declared nonhome region. On success, capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone; trade does not exhaust ships. Fill as many as possible: first writer goes to home port; each later order extends the connected route filled in this Trade. Other Presidencies’ writers cannot extend it, and writers do not limit capacity—use available writers, then filled-order tokens. Cannot fill another President’s home region. President gets £1 per order and writer owners £1 per placed writer; Balance gains printed order revenue, or half rounded down if a firm filled it that turn. At most one successful Trade per President per turn; failed attempts may retry during its uninterrupted opportunity if affordable.

Deploy may target own Presidency home, associated regions, or any region bordering an associated region; never another home or another Presidency’s Company region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and active local alliances for printed strength, then subtract the target and all other regions in its empire (target counted once; Company defense is zero). After every attempt, roll one die per exhausted officer; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments do not roll losses. Noncatastrophic failures may retry with remaining resources.

On success, loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers plus one for Commander. Distribute repeatedly: Commander family first (£1 for Commander and each own surviving used officer); other families clockwise (£1 per used surviving officer); bank last (£1 per used regiment and each used alliance piece). Repeat cycles until loot is gone. Commander gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower/dome (and all matching flags in India if it was capital), open all target orders/remove unrest, put new-conquest control token above associated President box, overlay in region and only office card in Vacant Offices; if Elephant faced outward from target, move it inside. On catastrophe Commander returns half family trophies rounded up and member to supply; exhausted officers still check loss; Commander has no office card to vacate.

Governor takes printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls current pool without penalty, then reduces it by one regardless of result. Success earns £1, or £2 if immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one: build one ship stage, commission one regiment to associated President’s Army, or add an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President’s treasury. Each Tax after first this turn adds regional unrest. Any unsuccessful attempt adds one regional unrest; catastrophe also removes Governor. Continue with shrinking pool until stopping, no dice, or catastrophe. Ship construction takes two successes: first places partial ship in region, next completes it into associated President’s sea zone.

Expenses are £1 per Debt, each Army officer/regiment, and each ship in sea zones including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance is short, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until track end; continue taking them even at maximum Debt. New emergency Debt adds no current-turn expense. After loans Balance is set to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance to expectations for current Standing and lower Standing one if short. Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1 per Company share; each owner including Chairman gets £1 per share. If total dividend cash strictly exceeds expectations, raise Standing one.

A primary Crisis against a Company region is resolved first; then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, ordered Bombay→Madras→Bengal, with that Presidency’s Commander choosing order within it. Primary normal Crisis strength includes unrest in target; primary Foreign Invasion uses only ordinary attack die; each secondary strength is only its region’s unrest. Associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling that strength, or as many as possible. The printed test says defense succeeds if newly exhausted pieces do not equal strength; a matched defense removes all target unrest and awards Commander a trophy. If it defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. For an indivisible alliance exceeding required strength, the summary says the ruling is unresolved. If Commander vacant, Military Affairs acts, or Chairman if that office is vacant; they choose defense and do not gain/lose trophies.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Attacks on Company; unresolved source gap.

answers.answer: Support −1 or less fails: discard law; resolve dilemma If Failed text; Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM shifts proposed policy one adjacent space either way and resolves it. Zero or more passes: place law with passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy, then immediate law effects. Restore used vote cards after either result. If law causes Company failure, finish the vote before scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at start of turn before London Season, PM may call a special vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary vote/support rules with exceptions: pass lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM passed-law token and activates firms; fail raises Company share scoring value one step (Court token, max ±3). No policy; failure neither removes PM nor discards Deregulation law, and PM may vote against. 1813 starts deregulated.

Only a player currently managing no firm may form one: return eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side, flip family board to firm charter, place family member as first firm share, set value to leftmost space, and take £5 from bank into London treasury. Invest with manager consent using Company share or workshop contribution; bank pays £5 into London. Up to ten firm shares; later investments still add £5 but create no share. Cannot contribute Chairman share, any Company share while Standing or Debt on lined space, or a share created this turn even if traded away. Invested workshops stay invested if firm fails and lose bonus/failure VP.

Each firm gets one trade attempt per turn and needs at least one ship to select a trade strategy (may choose closed home port); Hobnob has no bid/trade/dividends. Managers secretly select strategy and London bid; reveal bids together but keep strategies facedown until Presidency begins. There roll one die per committed £1 and pay bid to bank; any 1/2 permits trade. Initiative is ships minus successful dice (1s/2s); a President’s successful trade initiative is calculated likewise. Fill lowest initiative first; President resolves ties, and Company is not automatically first. If President is vacant or never succeeds, firms fill after Commander/Governors’ chance and Chairman breaks ties. Fill open orders only, up to ships+1, from chosen home port along own filled route. A firm may refill any order already filled this turn; previously filled order pays half revenue rounded down. Advance firm Value one per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.

At Revenue firms act before Company in initiative order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus higher of share count or firm Value, paid from London and/or India. If unable, dissolve unless rescued by normal-rule emergency investments or emergency merger. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards and charter to family side; invested workshops stay invested. After expenses manager may pay dividends from India only: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. A shareholder waiving payment needs manager consent. Record total actual cash paid out on Balance track. Sweep remaining India cash to London.

Components are limited; when supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Public information includes discards and family cash; facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids during selection are temporarily concealed.

Negotiable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares, promise cards. Not negotiable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. Transfer a share by returning old owner’s member and replacing it at share location with receiver-family member. Blackmail may be traded only facedown; played faceup blackmail cannot be traded.

Immediate transfers are binding; future-behavior promises are not, except a printed promise card’s guaranteed effect may be called if possible. Calls follow card timing/limits; no calls during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which. Promise cards may transfer to a third party or guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (for example a workshop paid this bonus phase does not pay again after sale that phase).

Use the scenario player setup cards, adding three extra cards for five players or six for six players; shuffle/deal evenly. Take listed cash, enterprises and positions and place listed holdings using setup placement rules; each office holder gets matching office card. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Remaining office cards are set aside distinguishing vacant offices from not-yet-created offices. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together, deal three London display cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown); shuffle remaining laws.

Game ends at scenario’s final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; if during Events, finish that phase; if caused by legislation, finish vote. Stop negotiations, promises and blackmail after game over unless card explicitly permits final-scoring use; no negotiations or promise calls during Final Scoring.

Power total combines enterprise/share power from current Power track (bottom two positions zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 for PM, and printed card power including faceup/down blackmail and applicable spouse. Power awards depend on final turn: 3/1 VP on turns 1–3, 5/2 turns 4–6, 8/4 turns 7–8. Tied first each get only lower award; no other award; tied second get none. Highest final VP wins; tie-break most windows, then clockwise from PM.

If Company survives, each Company share adds current Court VP; if failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Before either branch each shareholder may make one eligible special retirement from supply, whether Company survives or fails; this firm retirement is not replaced by a failure card. Then survived: roll office attrition and retire Pensioners without display cards. Failed: instead draw one random Company failure card. Firm share scoring and Debtor’s Prison deductions are scored separately beforehand.

Spouses generally add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot transfer. Required enterprise/share trades happen immediately on taking spouse. Retirement discounts can stack, are personal, and each may be used once per London Season and once during Final Scoring.

If a shipyard returns because of Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship remains in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.

Luxury: pay £4, gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, window icon; social enterprise. Shipyard: £2, take shipyard and matching ship unfitted on it; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Workshop: £5, take workshop; manufacturing enterprise, two votes and £1 bonus; worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Enlist Writer: put member in any Presidency Writers box; with at least four vacant offices, one additional writer once this turn. Enlist Officer: put member in Officers-in-Training. Seek Share: place member at empty Stock Exchange space and pay bank queue price £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5; it is applicant until share creation.

If a family piece must be placed with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose its printed VP; also applies to firm-share creation. If no Family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.
If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman. Place a member from supply, or if needed take one from a prize (lose its VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman.

Chairman hires Director of Trade (current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer), Manager of Shipping (any writer), Military Affairs (Presidential Commander, else any officer, else trainee), and China Superintendent (any writer; immediately on creation). Director hires Presidents (writer or Governor associated with that Presidency); each associated President hires its Governor (writer or officer in region; Commander ineligible). Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way as Director. Ordinary own-family hires need pool consent, except Chairman election and Commander appointment.

Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 treasury per die with no penalty. Success opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China (place overlay/card; Chairman immediately hires any writer). After all Envoys, may transfer up to two writers or ships between any Presidencies/sea zones including China. Cannot transfer while still taking Envoys.

Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers, each an officer or regiment between Armies, remaining in top half. Then assign every trainee to any Army’s top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if vacant or another family has more total Army pieces than incumbent’s family, choose among families with most pieces; move selected officer to Commander slot and previous Commander to top as officer. A tie with incumbent family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

Each President chooses the order of its Commander, Governors and own Trade; each position gets an opportunity, though Commander/Governors may decline. A position completes all actions before next; Trade may go before or after other positions but cannot interrupt. If President vacant, Chairman only sets order and cannot trade or approve local-alliance purchases.

Trade ships do not exhaust. At nonfinal Refresh writers return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade; Upkeep and Refresh.

answers.answer: At start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request President treasury funds for printed-price local alliances; President must approve. Move purchased pieces to active top half. Deploy or defense exhausts whole alliance to bottom; printed strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split between purposes. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too; unlike officers/regiments they do not reactivate. Excess alliance strength handling in defense is unresolved by summary.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy; Attacks on Company; source gap.

answers.answer: Company defense penalty is zero. Since no tower remains, there are zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, loot is minimum surviving participating officers plus one for Commander, then distributed normally.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy → already Company-controlled region.

answers.answer: Successful build requires two separate Governor successes: first success places partial ship in the region; second success completes it into sea zone associated with Governor’s President. Partial ship has no other effect. Each commissioned regiment is placed in Army associated with that President; it has officer-like strength, loot paid to bank, and no officer-loss rolls.

Successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law creates China; Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping/Director may send ships there. It acts after Bengal; its ships count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.

China gets one attempt only, including a failed attempt; roll one die per ship. If no export icon exists in Company-controlled regions, do not attempt. On success count export icons in all Company-controlled regions only: Company Balance gets £4 per icon and Superintendent’s family gets £1 per icon from bank. No non-Company icons count.

When Governor General law creates office: all Governors become pensioners, overlays and partial ships are removed, Governor/Director cards return to box; replace Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue and put ribbon overlay. Conquests create no Governors/overlays; printed Company symbols mark control. Governor General hires Presidents, uses Director treasury/turn position, is hired like Director and rolls attrition. Region loss skips Governor elimination.

First add £3 Balance per Company region. Then Govern attempts may repeat, paying £1 treasury per die, no penalty; at most one success per turn. Each rolled 6 adds one unrest to every Company region, even on success; failure adds another unrest to every Company region. On success gain £1 per Company region and choose exactly one benefit per region: complete ship to any sea zone including China; regiment to any Army; or £2 to Balance/any office treasury except own, adding unrest to a Company region. This turn’s Tax choices must add unrest to different regions.

Roll storm die; in indicated zone(s), roll once per player-owned ship: 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue (or sink if already fatigued), 5–6 sink. Sunk ship returns to shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are storm-exempt; China counts Eastern. Firm ships face storms in chosen strategy zone; Hobnob ships are exempt.

When order newly closes, return any writer there to owner’s supply; flip filled token to closed. If order is in already fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to its orders; if a connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead. If none open, it also Cascades. A region may initiate Cascade only once per event tile but can receive multiple Cascade effects.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Closing orders and Cascades.

answers.answer: Turmoil closes northernmost open order in top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. Windfall gives owners £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and each bordering region. Shuffle: March Elephant, shuffle event with remaining draw stack, separately shuffle discards and put them on top; if draw stack empty, March last instead.

Leader: top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. If dominated, instead it rebels with printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events in India event table → Leader.

answers.answer: Peace with Elephant on border opens orders connected across border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March in either case.
answers.evidence: Events in India event table → Peace.

answers.answer: Sovereign attacker’s whole empire strength plus modifier must be strictly greater than defender’s whole empire strength; ties fail. On success replace defender flag with attacker’s dominated flag; taking capital shatters its empire. If attacker lacks empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none available, no new empire/flags form.

Compare only rebelling region strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions do not count. Must be strictly greater, so tie fails. On success actor becomes sovereign, its flag is removed and all its orders close (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from capital.

Commander returns half family trophies rounded up, then member to supply; roll once per officer in associated Army, each 6 removes officer. Governor card/fatigue/member return to unused stack/supply, overlay removed; remove partial ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Control token returns to region loot-side down, region-symbol up. Rebellion/Foreign Invasion close orders; normal Invasion closes all or Cascades if already closed. Standing loss by regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second additional −2, etc. A lost region does not automatically lose others; resolve their attacks/defenses separately.

After successful Invasion Crisis, move Elephant to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise move to top-stack region. In Company region place it fully inside; in dominated region point toward sovereign; in sovereign region point across shape-marked border. If neighbor already dominated by actor, use first clockwise neighbor not so dominated; if all are, use redirect-arrow border toward empire capital.

Foreign Invasion targets based on storm die: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means each, none means top-stack region. Roll ordinary die per target for attack. On success close all target orders (Cascade if already closed), remove target flag and matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, set towers to half ordinary attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Unrest does not add to primary attack or tower strength; primary uses ordinary attack die and Company defense procedure applies.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Foreign Invasion; FAQ → Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law, revealing sequentially. After one or two ordinary draws, may stop or continue up to three; choose any revealed law and discard others. Drawing dilemma forces choosing it and ends drawing. Before voting PM moves dial clockwise or counterclockwise, stopping at first policy space matching selected law’s bottom icon; that determines target/consequence.

Tax: each family pays bank £1 per target owned; unpaid targets return to supply, including Chairman if taxed. Window tax additionally costs each window on enterprises and each prize member; return unpaid enterprise/prize member. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per target owned. Power: swap target marker with next higher; if already highest, swap any other pair.

Starting PM, clockwise, each casts votes: £1 family cash per vote plus printed card votes. Each card’s votes usable once across the entire vote, not again in later rounds; rotate when used and leave until resolution. PM may call another full round or stop after each; round with no votes ends voting.

A supporter may later oppose, but once opposed cannot vote for during this vote. Track opposition totals; largest opponent holds Opposition Leader, tied current holder retains. With recipient consent, votes can be cast for an already-opposed or committing-to-oppose player and count toward their opposition. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprise opposition except forced ‘Vote with my enterprises’ promise.

Prize upkeep is paid in Upkeep even on final turn. Pay separately for each member; if unpaid, return member and lose printed prize VP. Final turn skips Refresh and goes to scoring. Nonfinal Refresh returns writers to associated Presidency Writers boxes; filled tokens/dividers and extra ships to supply; reactivates exhausted Army officers/regiments; exhausts active alliances without reactivating; fitted player ships retain fatigue.

Each shareholder may make one additional retirement from supply each London Season, regardless of how many firms they own shares in. Actual post-discount cash spent may not exceed highest total dividend marker among their firms; printed prize cost may be higher if spouse discounts cover difference. Cannot retire from firm with absent or zero marker. At Final Scoring start, score firms then allow one special retirement regardless of Company outcome, before normal scoring; no display cards.

Investment £5 from bank goes to London; trade revenues go to India. London pays for ship fitting (£3 bank), bids (to bank) and can help pay expenses. India pays dividends and can help pay expenses; after dividends remaining India cash sweeps to London. Family cash cannot move into/out of firm treasuries except the specified procedures; no arbitrary gifts/transfers.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → firm investments; Firm expenses, rescue and dividends; Cash location matters.

answers.answer: Firms phase is after Family share creation and before Hiring; investment actions continue until nobody wants more, then strategies are chosen. Manager resolves timing conflicts within firm; PM resolves conflicts between firms.

Firm may fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 from London to bank with shipyard owner consent. May buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid to Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships. No support for fitting another player’s shipyard ship without consent; fitting requires consent.

Only a player managing no firm may initiate; managing another firm also disqualifies. Need consent of holders of majority of target shares. Move target ships, money and shares to new charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

Managers negotiate with every shareholder’s consent. Highest-value firm is primary; tied highest allows players to choose. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family side. Negotiate transfers and any shares over ten with owners’ consent. One binding immediate transfer; primary value/dividend track continues.
Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends; still pays expenses and retains previous dividend marker for retirement. Its ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade; firm expenses, rescue and dividends.

answers.answer: At ten shares, additional emergency investment can still contribute funds under normal share/workshop investment rules but creates no share; emergency investment pays expenses, loses any remaining cash and lowers Value one per emergency investment. Same-turn Company shares remain ineligible to invest even if traded away. The summary does not specify how “unused rescue cash” beyond those stated procedures is handled beyond loss of remaining cash in an emergency investment.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends; Firms investments.

answers.answer: Emergency merger is with only ONE other firm. Normal merger procedure applies, including every involved shareholder’s consent. Other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.

Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. Use insolvent-firm procedure: shares go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to matching shipyards, charter flips to family side. Invested workshops remain invested for rest of game.
answers.evidence: Firms phase → Voluntary dissolution; Firm expenses.

answers.answer: For each player separately, add VP from all their shares across all firms, then round that player’s total down once; afterward deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. This firm scoring occurs before normal Company survived/failed branch, so applies either way.

1710 runs turns 1–5, starts monopoly/no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs turns 3–7, starts monopoly and deregulation may be voted in. 1813 runs turns 5–8, starts deregulated. Long 1710 runs turns 1–8, same initial position as 1710 with deregulation available.

1710: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, £3 each office treasury, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12, Debt 3, £4 treasury each, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship East Indian, Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

1813: Standing £10, Debt 0, £3 each office treasury; Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in Presidencies; return Governor General law to box and place overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors.
Power award: turns 1–3 first/second 3/1 VP; turns 4–6 5/2; turns 7–8 8/4. If tied first, each tied player receives only the lower (second-place) award and no other award.

Initial Power: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. In 1758/Long 1710 special Deregulation vote may be called if Standing and/or Debt on lined space, must if either is starred. Standing expectations are £4/6/8/10/12/14/16; S is above £10. Deregulation lines: Standing £4/6/8 and Debt 5/6/7/8; Standing £4 and Debt 8 starred.

No. Designer ruling says unrest does not increase Foreign Invasion primary strength or resulting tower level. Use ordinary die both for attack strength and to set towers at half rounded down. On successful event, close all target orders once; if already all closed, Cascade. Region Loss does not close them a second time.

If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it fails. Company Fraud at start of Revenue rolls one die per your officeholder, reduces Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), and pays from bank only amount actually removed from Balance. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demoted Commander is eligible as officer for reappointment.

Set Balance to £5 and family VP markers to zero. Put local alliances in named Army boxes; money-side-up loot tokens in matching regions. Choose scenario and follow card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and India map; set Turn marker to its starting date and PM dial arm to matching date. Exact map details are read from scenario card (summary does not reproduce the full map configuration).
answers.evidence: Setup; Components → India terminology; Scenario figures.

answers.answer: Normal order: London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation votes occur at very start before London Season. Skip London Season on game’s first turn.

Retirement order starts with Chairman, or former Chairman if office vacant, then clockwise. Each player may retire each Pensioner to a prize: pay its printed cost, move member to prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display order, then pay bank. Pensioners need not all be retired; unused Pensioners return to supply after Prestige step.

No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital’s starred flag, so it is no longer an empire. Applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.

answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Firm-track VP per share.
